sources.title: Critical Percolation, Scaling, and Long-Range Models
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: A broad route through critical phenomena, general inequalities, mean-field mechanisms, planar multipoint geometry, and long-range renormalisation.
sources.coverageNote: Selected correspondences for this prototype. The snapshot has 10 numbered chapters, 45 named statements and definitions, and 698 outer displayed-math blocks. These are document counts, not a complete assertion census or verified-proof count.

sources.title: Percolation
sources.author: Geoffrey Grimmett
sources.edition: Second edition · Springer · provisional project edition
sources.description: A baseline for classical percolation: basic techniques, phase transitions, subcritical and supercritical theory, renormalisation, critical phenomena, planar theory, and extensions.
sources.coverageNote: Chapter-level navigation samples only. The complete edition-specific inventory, including exercises and precise claims in prose, remains to be made. No claim of book-level formal coverage is made here.

sources.title: Progress in High-Dimensional Percolation and Random Graphs
sources.author: Markus Heydenreich and Remco van der Hofstad
sources.edition: Springer book; chapter locators below checked against the author manuscript of 17 March 2017
sources.description: A route from the basic model to mean-field mechanisms, lace expansion, the IIC, finite-size scaling, random graphs, and related models.
sources.coverageNote: Selected chapter-level links, not a statement census. Published-edition pagination and theorem numbering must be reconciled with the accessible author manuscript. Exercises, survey material, and open problems remain in scope.

sources.title: The Lean mathematical library
sources.author: The mathlib community
sources.description: The existing Lean dependency of lrp, providing reusable foundations for measures, independent coordinates, graphs, sums, and analysis.
sources.coverageNote: The pinned library supplies the underlying measure, graph and analytic APIs. Source inspection and a dependency pin do not establish compiled proof status or prose correspondence; those are read from the supplied manifest and matching review records.

sources.title: The critical two-point function for long-range percolation on the hierarchical lattice
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: Averaged and pointwise critical connection estimates on the hierarchical lattice.
sources.coverageNote: Version-specific reading map: 1.1–1.6 and 2.1–2.14, including remarks, are inventoried in wiki/sources/hierarchical-2103.17013v1.md. This is not complete prose coverage or a formal correspondence certificate. Existing article statements and tags are unchanged.

sources.title: A new proof of the sharpness of the phase transition for Bernoulli percolation and the Ising model
sources.author: Hugo Duminil-Copin and Vincent Tassion
sources.description: A finite-size criterion and differential-inequality route to sharpness.
sources.coverageNote: The percolation statements are a source for the planned shared critical theory. The prototype does not include a Lean implementation of the finite-size criterion or the sharpness proof.

sources.title: On the derivation of mean-field percolation critical exponents from the triangle condition
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: Quantitative implications of triangle-diagram control, including slowly diverging diagrams.
sources.coverageNote: Partial source map in wiki/sources/. The boundary, derivative, transcript-entropy and Fourier-duality diagnoses in the errata are provisional and await Tom’s confirmation; their locators refer to arXiv v3, not an unchecked journal edition.

sources.title: Power-law bounds for critical long-range percolation below the upper-critical dimension
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: Critical long-range estimates and universal finite-graph tools that serve several parts of the library.
sources.coverageNote: The threshold-bound locator refers to the arXiv v2 Introduction. Published version: DOI 10.1007/s00440-021-01043-7; edition equivalence and published pagination are not certified. Universal tightness is a separate formalisation target.

sources.title: Percolation Inequalities and Decision Trees
sources.author: Nikita Gladkov
sources.description: Decision-tree inequalities and S-disjoint constructions used in finite and countable multipoint percolation bounds.
sources.coverageNote: Definition 4.2 and the applications in Theorem 5.2, Corollary 5.3 and Section 6.1 were checked on the primary PDF on 19 November 2026. The two local notation/direction discrepancies are provisional; this is not a claim that the adaptive decision-tree theorem or every displayed multipoint bound has been formalized.

sources.title: Critical long-range percolation I: High effective dimension
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: High-dimensional cluster laws and spatial scaling through a real-space analysis of cutoff models.
sources.coverageNote: The version-specific reading map covers cutoff spatial moments and the passage to large-volume conditioning. The wiki gives the normalized Euclidean d > 3 alpha spatial-moment limit under explicit endpoint assumptions; the canonical cutoff-removal argument retains its continuum construction and moment-formula inputs. Other model regimes, full prose coverage and source correspondence remain incomplete.

sources.title: Critical long-range percolation II: Low effective dimension
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: Localisation, multipoint inequalities, and the geometry of the low-dimensional long-range regime.
sources.coverageNote: Initial version-specific reading map under wiki/sources/; source contracts and full coverage remain unfinished.

sources.title: Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension
sources.author: Tom Hutchcroft
sources.description: Critical-dimensional logarithmic corrections and the hydrodynamic input for long-range scaling.
sources.coverageNote: A source link in the prototype, not a completed theorem inventory. This upper-critical regime is distinct from the alpha = 2 marginal lace-expansion regime.

sources.title: PercolationAudit
sources.author: Ahmed Bou-Rabee; development with ChatGPT and Claude, building on Anthropic PercolationContinuity
sources.description: An audited Lean percolation development. The lrp adaptation reuses selected Bernoulli and site-connectivity foundations with retained source notices.
sources.coverageNote: Upstream source, CI and comparator evidence have been inspected. Selected foundations have been ported to lrp’s pinned toolchain; see the reused-library register for the exact build evidence and scope. The upstream criticality certificate is not imported by this small port.

sources.coverageNote: The reported discrepancy in Lemma 5.3 is provisional and awaits Tom’s confirmation; the bubble-only correction remains unresolved.
